items.review_rationale: Reviewed inverse-image characterization of continuous function between topological spaces, including universal quantification over target open sets and requiring the preimage open in the source.

references.context: Set of all x in domain X whose image f(x) belongs to target subset V.
Membership of inverse image in source topology for every target open set.

references.phrase: continuity for all target open sets
references.disposition: Global preimage criterion is equivalent to the pointwise neighborhood criterion for topological continuity.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed neighborhood characterization of continuity at every point of the domain, requiring matching open neighborhoods and containment of the image f(U) in V, not merely pointwise membership.

references.context: Open subset U of X containing the selected point x.
Open subset V of Y containing the image of x.
For every x and target open neighborhood V, some domain open neighborhood U satisfies f(U) subset V.

references.disposition: This second formulation describes the same continuous-map meaning rather than a prerequisite on its sibling formulation.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed discrete topology on the source-specified nonempty set S by identifying its open sets with the entire power set; not generalized to empty domain by this independent source.

references.phrase: every subset of S is open

references.context: Family comprising all subsets of the underlying set S.
A set containing at least one element as explicitly required by this sourced formulation.

references.disposition: Every subset is open here, unlike an arbitrary topology; empty-space permissibility is not inferred.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed finite-generation characterization of Noetherian A-module, quantifying over every A-submodule and retaining the commutative unital coefficient-ring convention.

references.phrase: unital left module M over A

references.context: Underlying ring structure with additive commutativity, multiplicative commutativity and specified identity.

references.disposition: Noetherianity requires finite generation of all submodules, not only finite generation of M itself.
